edit.description: add stop to SUBCOMMANDS/HELP_TOP; handler writes <flumeDir>/stop idempotently and prints the consequence; flume status gains a stop-flag line between supervisor liveness and tip claim; flume loop (and job run) refuses at start, exit 1 naming the path, when the flag is already present.

superviseLoop checks the stop flag at the same per-iteration boundary it re-reads the baton (never mid-tick); on seeing it, ends the run after the in-flight tick finishes and releases the claim/lock; SuperviseResult records why iteration ended for the completion summary, without changing loopExitCode's totals-based formula.
flume stop is idempotent and prints the consequence; flume status reports the flag; flume loop refuses at start with the flag present.
a stop flag written mid-run lets the in-flight tick finish, then ends the run and releases the claim/lock.

summary: flume stop writes <flumeDir>/stop; the supervisor finishes its in-flight tick then ends the run; a present flag refuses a fresh loop/job run start until removed.
tests: flume stop is idempotent — repeat call prints the same statement, exit 0
flume loop refuses to start with the flag already present, naming the path, exit 1
a stop flag written between tick children ends the run after the current tick finishes, without killing it
flume tick ignores the flag and runs normally
a stopped run's exit code still reflects run totals (errored/shipped), not a special stop code
acceptance: flume stop/status/loop behave per spec: idempotent write, checked only at the baton-reread boundary, refuse-at-start, no kill, no unstop verb, exit code unchanged by the stop path itself.
notes: Also spec/cli.md: Subcommand surface (stop verb) and 'flume status owes exactly this' (status line #3). Deliberately no unstop/resume verb — removing the flag is the operator's own ack.

edit.description: defaultTickRunner passes FLUME_TIP_CLAIM_HELD=<supervisor pid> in each spawned tick child's env.

flume tick: when FLUME_TIP_CLAIM_HELD is absent, acquire+release its own tip claim around the single tick, refusing exit 1 on a live foreign claim; when present, trust the supervisor's claim and take none itself.
a bare flume tick acquires and releases its own claim, refusing when another live process holds it.
a loop-spawned tick child does not re-acquire the claim its supervisor already holds.

summary: A bare flume tick now takes its own tip claim around the single tick; a loop-spawned child trusts the supervisor's claim via FLUME_TIP_CLAIM_HELD instead of probing pids.

per.section: The loop lock and the tip claim

tests: a bare flume tick with no other live claim-holder acquires and releases a claim around its single tick
a bare flume tick refuses exit 1 when a live process already holds the claim
a loop child spawned with FLUME_TIP_CLAIM_HELD set does not call acquireTipClaim itself
acceptance: Every tick — bare or loop-spawned — runs under exactly one live claim; a loop child never double-acquires, and a bare tick is no longer claimless.
notes: Closes the claimless-bare-tick gap: previously only loop-level ticks were guarded, leaving concurrent bare ticks to collide with only optimistic tip-verify between them.
